blocks.text: Éditions Odyssée publishes Anne Garde: Géographie du regard ( Geography of the Gaze ) , a monograph produced in partnership with the MPP – Médiathèque du patrimoine et de la photographie (Heritage and Photography Library).

“For Anne, the camera or view camera, the choice of viewpoint and framing count for nothing without the magic of the instant when, through a strange chemical reaction, light turns into an image on the transparent surface of the film as the shutter is released. It is through mastering these chemical and luminous chances that Anne came to photography.” – Gilles Désiré dit Gosset and Matthieu Rivallin MPP

An exceptional artist and technician, Anne Garde holds a singular place in the contemporary photographic landscape. Since the 1980s, she has developed a free-spirited body of work at the crossroads of an “inhabited photography” and an “augmented photography,” a practice that uses ephemeral installations to reveal places that are often marginal or unusual.

Alongside Laure Vernière, her partner in life, writing and travel, she travels the world where commissions and subjects take her. From Central Asia to China and on to India of a thousand faces, she unrolls a thread of red silk for Hermès and photographs the palaces of maharajas and nawabs, and contemporary architecture in Brazil and New York…

Nourished by these experiences and colors, she casts a renewed eye on the submarine base of Bordeaux (her native city), the bunkers of the Atlantic coast, the silent architecture of the Palais de Tokyo and the Palais de Chaillot, and also the shipyards of Chittagong in Bangladesh, where the great ships of globalization are dismantled by hand.

Like a travel notebook, this monograph rearranges the fragments and memories of these photographic narratives. It traces the path of an artist attentive to the traces, absences and metamorphoses of the real, whose images reveal, in the words of journalist and writer Pierre Veilletet, “the corrupted underside of beauty.”
